standard_prerequisites.name: The Gysin pullback of a principal divisor on an integral scheme, and additivity of capping with a first Chern class
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-gysin-factors-general (proof line 5457) and lemma-c1-cap-additive (proof line 5459)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first identifies the Gysin pullback of the divisor of a rational function with the cap of the first Chern class of the structure sheaf of the divisor with the fundamental class, and the second observes that this cap is the zero map.

core_obligations: Reduce to a single integral scheme: write a rationally trivial cycle as a locally finite sum of pushforwards of principal divisors along integral subschemes of dimension k + 2, form the disjoint union of those subschemes, use the compatibility of the Gysin map with the proper pushforward from that union, and the fact that the pushforward along the union factors through rational equivalence, to reduce to the case where X is integral and the cycle is a single principal divisor (proof lines 5429-5448).

Dispose of the case where the divisor is everything: if X equals D then the Gysin pullback of the principal divisor is the cap of the Chern class of the invertible sheaf with that divisor, which is rationally trivial by the statement that capping with a first Chern class factors through rational equivalence (proof lines 5451-5454).

Dispose of the proper divisor case: if the divisor is strictly smaller than X, then the Gysin pullback of the principal divisor equals the cap of the Chern class of the structure sheaf of the divisor with the fundamental class of the divisor, and capping with the Chern class of the structure sheaf is the zero map (proof lines 5455-5459).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an integral X and a principal divisor by the base change along the disjoint union of the components (proof lines 5429-5448).
Case X = D: reduce to a cap with a first Chern class, which factors through rational equivalence (proof lines 5451-5454).
Case D strictly smaller: rewrite as a cap with the Chern class of the structure sheaf, which is zero (proof lines 5455-5459).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the Gysin homomorphism attached to a triple descends from cycles to the Chow group (statement lines 5419-5427, tag 02TO). The proof is a real reduction: it unfolds rational equivalence into a locally finite sum of principal divisors, uses the compatibility of the Gysin map with the proper pushforward from the disjoint union of the components to reduce to an integral scheme with a single principal divisor, and then splits into the two cases according to whether the divisor is the whole scheme, in which case the first Chern class statement applies, or a proper divisor, in which case the Gysin pullback is a cap with the Chern class of the structure sheaf and therefore vanishes. The two-case analysis is the substance, so the claim is H2.
